results.intent: Splice a two-perspective independent investigation fan-out with a deterministic consolidation step between the anchor implementation and the existing review gate.
assumptions: "This problem" in the operator instruction means the goal implemented at the anchor node N01, not a separate question supplied out of band.
The operator did not name the two perspectives, so they were chosen as correctness/behaviour versus risk/integration — two lenses that fail in different ways rather than two copies of the same check.

Parallelism is expressed structurally: the anchor is switched to ALL_MATCHES so both unconditional outgoing edges fire and the two investigations run as independent branches. The planner cannot author concurrency directly.

expected_incoming on the MERGE node is expressed as edge ids (E_N10_N12, E_N11_N12), matching the rule's wording that it must equal the edges arriving at the node. If the runtime expects node ids there, this needs a mechanical rewrite to ["N10", "N11"].
The investigation nodes are typed REVIEW because that is the only closed-set type for read-only analysis; they are not gates and produce findings, not routing decisions.
The existing route N01 -> N02 is preserved in order, not replaced: the review still runs, now downstream of the consolidation.
warnings: Switching the anchor to ALL_MATCHES changes routing semantics for N01 as a whole, not just for these two edges. Confirm no other behaviour depends on N01 being FIRST_MATCH before accepting.

The two investigation nodes are typed REVIEW but route unconditionally, so any `verdict` they emit gates nothing. N02 remains the only gate on this route. If the runtime requires a REVIEW node's verdict to be consumed, these nodes will emit an unread verdict.

Pre-existing and untouched by this proposal: N02 declares only an E_N02_PASS edge. A verdict of REPAIR or BLOCKED at N02 has no declared route. Feeding N02 a consolidated findings list makes a non-PASS verdict more likely, so this gap is more likely to be hit after accepting than before.

ALL_REQUIRED on N12 means a stalled or failed investigation branch blocks consolidation and therefore blocks the review. There is no FALLBACK edge around N12; add one, or accept that a single dead branch stalls the route.

This adds three nodes and at least two additional agent invocations to every pass through the graph. Check the remaining headroom against the workflow's max_llm_calls (16) and max_nodes (16) limits, particularly if repair cycles re-enter this section.

Independence of the two investigations is asserted in their instructions, not enforced by the graph. If the runtime shares context between sibling branches, the two perspectives will correlate and the fan-out buys less than it appears to.

nodes.instructions:
Investigate the problem addressed by the anchor implementation from a correctness perspective, independently. Do not consult, wait for, or reconcile with the other investigation running alongside you; divergence between the two is the point of running both.

Work read-only. Do not edit anything, do not stage or revert anything, and do not alter the candidate.

Establish what the intended behaviour is, where the implemented work satisfies it, and where it does not. Cover stated acceptance criteria, boundary and empty-input cases, and behaviour the tests assert versus behaviour they only appear to assert.

Record each finding as a short claim, the component or behaviour it affects, and a severity drawn from the severity ladder. Substantiate every claim with what you actually observed; where you are uncertain, say so and leave it uncertain rather than resolving it by inference.

Do not propose or apply a fix. Do not judge the candidate as a whole: the downstream review owns the verdict, and your findings are an input to it, not a substitute for it.
acceptance: The investigation ran read-only and produced no edits.
Findings are recorded with an affected component and a severity, or the absence of findings is stated explicitly.
The investigation was conducted without reference to the parallel investigation's output.

Look at what the change touches rather than at what it claims: interactions with surrounding behaviour, regressions in paths that were previously working, error and failure handling, concurrency or ordering assumptions, and invariants that hold only on the happy path. Note scope that was widened beyond the stated goal as well as scope that was quietly dropped.

nodes.instructions:
Consolidate the two independent investigations into one set of findings. Both upstream investigations are required; do not proceed on a partial set.

Deduplicate findings that describe the same underlying issue, keeping the clearest statement of it and the higher of the two severities. Keep every finding that only one investigation raised: single-source is not the same as unsupported. Where the two investigations contradict each other, keep both positions and record the disagreement explicitly rather than choosing a winner.

Do not introduce findings that neither investigation raised, do not re-investigate, do not soften or escalate a severity beyond what its source assigned, and do not edit anything.

Emit one ordered list, most severe first, each entry carrying its affected component, its severity, and whether it came from one investigation or both. If both investigations came back empty, say so plainly instead of manufacturing content. This consolidated list is the sole findings input the downstream review consumes.
acceptance: Both upstream investigations completed and both were represented in the consolidation.
The output is a single deduplicated, severity-ordered list with no finding absent from both sources.
Contradictions between the two investigations are preserved and labelled rather than silently resolved.

Classify the scope of the candidate change in a fresh, read-only context. Do not edit files.

Determine whether the change touches anything under WORKFLOWS/ - any added, modified, renamed or deleted entry under that directory, at any depth.

Report has_findings = true when at least one touched entry lies under WORKFLOWS/, and has_findings = false otherwise. Report the touched entries your decision relied on so the routing is auditable.

You do not choose the next node: the deterministic gate routes on your report.
verdict = PASS when you established the scope with confidence.
verdict = BLOCKED when the scope cannot be established and a human decision is required.
acceptance: The scope classification ran in a fresh read-only context and no files were edited.
has_findings is true if and only if at least one touched entry lies under WORKFLOWS/.
The touched entries the decision relied on are reported.

nodes.instructions:
Perform the mandatory compliance review of the candidate change in a fresh, read-only context. Do not edit files.

Scope: the parts of the change that touch anything under WORKFLOWS/, plus their effect on the rest of the change. Check the change against the compliance requirements that govern workflow definitions in this repository, and record each requirement you checked together with the evidence for your conclusion. Where a requirement is unclear, or you cannot obtain the evidence needed to judge it, treat that as a human decision rather than guessing.

You do not choose the next node: set `verdict` and the deterministic gate routes.
verdict = PASS when every applicable compliance requirement is met.
verdict = REPAIR when the violations are concrete and correctable inside this candidate.
verdict = BLOCKED when a human decision is required, including when the applicable requirements cannot be established.
acceptance: The compliance review ran in a fresh read-only context and no files were edited.
Every applicable compliance requirement was checked and recorded with the evidence for its conclusion.
A verdict of PASS, REPAIR or BLOCKED is recorded against the candidate.

nodes.instructions:
Address the compliance findings raised against the candidate, in the isolated worktree.

Keep the change narrowly scoped to the reported violations, and add or update focused tests where a violation is testable. Do not broaden the original goal and do not undo unrelated parts of the candidate. Do not merge, push, create a PR, or alter the canonical checkout.

Record, per finding, what you changed, or why no change was required.
acceptance: Every compliance finding is either fixed in the isolated worktree or explicitly answered with a reason no change was required.
The change remains scoped to the reported violations and the original goal was not broadened.
The canonical checkout is untouched: nothing was merged, pushed or opened as a PR.

results.operator_instruction: Add a validation step on the hardening branch before it rejoins the migration branch at the merge.
results.expected: EXPECTED REFUSAL: splicing before M08 would change M08's protected expected_incoming set. A good planner declines or the validator refuses.
errors: M08: expected_incoming must exactly equal the graph's declared incoming edges (declared ['E_N05_CONTINUE', 'E_N06_CONTINUE'], graph has ['E_N06_CONTINUE', 'E_N10_MERGE'])

diagnostics.message: M08: expected_incoming must exactly equal the graph's declared incoming edges (declared ['E_N05_CONTINUE', 'E_N06_CONTINUE'], graph has ['E_N06_CONTINUE', 'E_N10_MERGE'])

results.intent: Splice one independent, non-mutating validation review into the hardening branch between the anchor N05 and the merge M08, so that only a validated hardening result rejoins the migration branch and anything else is routed to the existing human gate.
assumptions: "Validation step" is read as an independent, non-mutating review of the hardening branch, not a command-executing gate: MACHINE_GATE may not be proposed and a planner does not author a command line.
REVIEW nodes expose the verdict predicate key (PASS / REPAIR / BLOCKED), so PASS is the only condition under which the hardening branch is allowed to rejoin the merge.

The existing human gate N09 is the correct destination for a hardening result that does not pass validation, mirroring the existing FALLBACK from N04 (E_N04_FAILED) rather than introducing a new terminal.

Exactly one edge is routed into M08 from the hardening side, so the merge's incoming arity stays 2 and the harness may keep mutating merge_policy on M08 between ALL_REQUIRED and ANY_COMPLETED without changing merge arity.
The migration branch (N06 and its edge E_N06_CONTINUE into M08) is untouched, and N05 keeps FIRST_MATCH routing with a single unconditional outgoing edge declared last.
run_if ON_TRANSITION is used for the new node, matching every node in the supplied neighborhood.
warnings: M08 is an existing, immutable MERGE node whose expected_incoming names E_N05_CONTINUE, and this proposal detaches that edge. The graph rule that expected_incoming must exactly equal the edges arriving at a MERGE cannot be satisfied by a planner here: accepting this subgraph requires the operator to replace E_N05_CONTINUE with E_N10_MERGE in M08.expected_incoming (a one-for-one swap, order preserved). Until that edit is made, the resulting graph declares an empty slot and an undeclared incoming edge at M08 and should fail validation. Verify this before accepting.

Under merge_policy ALL_REQUIRED, a non-PASS validation sends the hardening branch to N09 and M08 never receives its hardening contribution, so the merge does not complete on that path. Under ANY_COMPLETED the migration branch alone satisfies the merge and execution continues. The two harness slices therefore diverge on the new non-PASS path; confirm that divergence is intended for the fixture before accepting.

No REPAIR lane is proposed for a REPAIR verdict. A repair node rejoining M08 would add a second incoming edge from the hardening side and change the merge's fixed arity, and a repair edge back into N05 or N10 would introduce a cycle. A REPAIR verdict therefore falls through the unconditional FALLBACK to N09 rather than being corrected in-branch, even though the workflow allows max_repair_cycles 2. If an in-branch repair lane is wanted, M08 has to be re-declared, which is outside planner authority.

Inserting a node on the hardening branch changes what the merge sees attributed to that branch, so base_semantic_hash 5fb0527b... is invalidated and any recorded merge_resolution_hash fixture for this slice will change. Regenerate the expected hashes for both the ALL_REQUIRED and ANY_COMPLETED variants.

The supplied neighborhood is truncated: N01 and N06 were not inspected. The assumption that the migration branch and the start node are unaffected by this splice has not been verified against their actual declarations.

This proposal adds one LLM-backed node to a workflow limited to 10 llm_calls and 12 nodes; node count becomes 7. Confirm the remaining call budget still covers the hardening branch plus any repair cycles.

nodes.instructions: Validate the hardening branch result before it rejoins the merge. Review the hardening change produced by the upstream branch against that branch's own acceptance criteria and against every carry_forward constraint in scope: the hardening must not widen the goal, must not introduce scope the branch was not given, and must not change behaviour beyond hardening. Report each problem as a finding with a severity, and record exactly one verdict: PASS when the hardening result is fit to be merged as-is, REPAIR when the problems found are correctable inside the hardening branch's scope, BLOCKED when validation cannot be completed or the result is unfit and cannot be corrected within scope. This node is read-only review: change nothing about the candidate, and do not carry migration-branch material into the judgement, since the hardening branch is the only input attributed to this node.
acceptance: The hardening branch result is reviewed against its acceptance criteria and its carry_forward constraints, and exactly one verdict is recorded.

The candidate is left unmodified by this node, so the merge still receives a single source-attributed hardening contribution.
